title: Payoff surface: chat SLA vs unit cost (working snapshot)
summary: Working snapshot: exploratory payoff-surface mapping for chat workloads. Shows discrete config points (quantization, batching, KV cache, routing) and an ASCII view of iso-cost / iso-latency contours. Intended for internal alignment and to seed a dashboard PRD.
body:
Purpose
This is a working snapshot to capture the 'payoff surface' for a representative chat workload: how incremental cost savings (per 1k queries) interact with delivered latency across common deployment knobs. Goal is to produce a simple artifact we can hand to Console/Optimize to turn into an interactive surface dashboard + a short narrative for sales collateral.

Context and constraints
- Workload: multi-turn customer support chat (avg turn 140 tokens, response length ~60 tokens).
- Baseline model: open-llama-13b-like baseline (fp16).
- Target metrics: p50 and p90 response latency (ms), dollars per 1k requests (hosted mode unit cost approximation).
- Knobs considered: quantization (fp16 -> int8/4-bit), batching strategy (small fixed batch vs dynamic multiplex), KV prefix cache (hitrate scenarios), routing (edge vs core), prewarm fraction.
- Important: numbers below are synthetic, from small lab sweep. Use for pattern detection, not absolute pricing.

Executive observations (short)
- Biggest single-step cost reduction without p50 regression: int8 quant with modest KV caching (hitrate 35-45%).
- Batching yields best amortized cost at the expense of tail; multiplex reduces p90 impact vs large static batches.
- Edge routing reduces p50 by 8-12ms for our EU region sample at ~6% cost premium; good for premium SLA tiers.
- There are clear 'knees' in the surface: small additional cost buys disproportionate tail latency improvements (likely worth for p90-focused SLAs).

Tabular sweep (representative points)
Config | quant | kv_hitrate | batching | route | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | cost($/1k)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A Baseline | fp16 | 0% | small-batch | core | 210 | 420 | 12.8
B Int8 + cache | int8 | 40% | small-batch | core | 220 | 450 | 7.6
C Int8 + cache + multiplex | int8 | 40% | multiplex | core | 230 | 300 | 7.4
D Int4 aggressive | int4 | 10% | multiplex | core | 250 | 390 | 5.3
E Edge routed premium | int8 | 40% | multiplex | edge | 210 | 280 | 8.1
F Prewarm 20% | int8 | 40% | multiplex + prewarm(20%) | core | 205 | 265 | 9.2
G Cache heavy | fp16 | 75% | small-batch | core | 190 | 360 | 9.6
H Hybrid: edge + int4 + cache | int4 | 45% | multiplex | edge | 205 | 290 | 5.9

Interpretation notes
- Compare A -> B: quantization alone reduces cost by ~40% but increases p50/p90 slightly; adding KV cache (B) mitigates tail with negligible cost change.
- C shows multiplexing trades p50 for dramatic p90 improvement vs B: explanation: multiplex reduces head-of-line batching penalties and spreads tokens across in-flight slots.
- D and H show int4 gets down to very low unit costs but p50 increases; pairing with edge routing or cache (H) recovers latency at low cost.
- F demonstrates prewarm buys latency (esp p50/p90) at a measurable cost — useful as a product offering for defined SLA tiers.

ASCII payoff-surface sketch (contours are approximate)
Legend: x-axis = p50 (ms), y-axis = cost ($/1k). Iso-p90 contours marked with labels.

cost ($/1k)
 12 |                      A (p90~420)
 10 |        G(190,9.6)      .            F(205,9.2)
  8 |          .   E(210,8.1)    B(220,7.6)
  6 |   H(205,5.9)  C(230,7.4)   D(250,5.3)
  4 |           .             .
     ------------------------------------------------> p50 (ms)
      180    200    220    240    260

Notes: visualizing shows two strands: a low-cost strand (int4/int8 aggressive) with higher p50 risk, and a premium low-latency strand (edge + prewarm) that sits at higher cost but low p50/p90. Ideal productization: expose this as a 2D surface with knobs as toggles.

Qualitative tradeoffs to call out for product copy
- "Pay for predictability": reserved prewarm + edge is premium but converts p90 risk into a concrete SKU.
- "Cost-first mode": aggressive quantization + multiplex is best for background or low-SLA customers.
- "Cache-first": for multi-turn assistant flows, KV cache delivers outsized tail improvements for moderate cost.

Open questions / next small experiments (priority ordered)
1) Full p99 sweep on the same configs (we only captured p50/p90). Hypothesis: prewarm reduces p99 more than p90. (JIRA-OPT-4422)
2) Evaluate quantization-induced quality regression on user eval sets for int4 vs int8 (linked to quality-adjusted cost per query work).
3) Measure edge regional variance: run EU, NA, and APAC to quantify edge cost premium vs latency delta.
4) Run microburst microbench with 1k-concurrent fanouts to capture slot contentions under multiplex.
5) Instrument cold-start distribution with prewarm fractions (0%, 10%, 20%, 50%).

Suggested product UX for dashboard
- X axis: p50 slider, Y axis: unit cost contour heatmap, toggles: quantization level, KV cache hitrate, batching mode, prewarm %.
- Hover card: shows expected p90/p99, delta vs baseline, recommended SKU and fallback policy.
- Quick compare mode: show two pinned points (e.g., "economy" vs "premium").

Short-term asks for teams
- Serving-runtime: add a metric flag to export multiplex slot occupancy per-second to the benchmarking surface (owner: Jun Park).
- Observability: produce a p99 sampling job for the listed configs (owner: Ayesha Khan).
- Product: prototype dashboard mock and spec (owner: Sofia Martinez).

Appendix: raw micro-sweep notes
- Sweep config: 3x 8-GPU nodes, synthetic client tails with 95th percentile user concurrency ~420; each config ran 20k requests.
- Measurement caveats: KV cache was simulated using recorded prefixes; we did not warm local OS caches between runs for conservative p50.
- Cost model: unit costs are extrapolated from hourly GPU equivalent + estimated infra egress + amortized model load costs; not billing-grade.

Action items (this doc)
- Convert this snapshot into a small interactive prototype (Figma + simple query surface) by 2029-07-12.
- Kick off JIRA-OPT-4422 and assign p99 sweep.
- Quick sync with Solutions Eng to get 3 customer profiles to validate: low-cost bot, mid-tier support assistant, regulated enterprise SLA.

Unresolved statements / TODOs
- Need confirmation on billing multipliers for edge routing in EU (finance).
- Decide whether int4 qualifies for hosted API beta or should be Dedicated-only.

Slack refs and related docs
- slack thread: #optimize-benchmarks: thread-334 (initial numbers posted 2029-06-18)
- Confluence page: CONFLUENCE-6789: "Payoff surfaces: methodology"
- Related JIRA: JIRA-OPT-4421 (dashboard PRD), JIRA-OPT-4422 (p99 sweep)

Footer
Working draft — please annotate inline or ping owners for corrections. Distribution: product-optimize, console-and-tooling, serving-runtime, observability.
